output.brief: The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.354%, and the upper edge of the normal band is 0.482%. Several earlier weeks were higher (0.51, 0.47, 0.45), and the three that were investigated turned up no fault. The burn rate is 0.82x, well under the 2x paging threshold. The dashboard counts match the raw logs. Booking completion didn't change and there were no customer complaints. The higher error rate on new pods during v4.18's rollout is cache warm-up, a known effect. The same gap appeared in all five recent rollouts, including a config-only redeploy, and it adds only 10–20 errors. So it is not evidence of a v4.18 fault. I did not rule out the replica move or partner-sync month-end load as small contributors, but at this size the evidence doesn't call for acting on them. Recommendation: don't roll back, don't mute alerting (muting would remove protection for no benefit), and don't move the replica. Record the week as within the normal band and apply the standard check to the next week. If next week exceeds 0.48% or the burn-rate page fires, open an incident then.
